categories.required-gpu: Portable compute or resource test. It must pass on the original Windows WARP baseline and through the live host adapter on every translated target profile.
categories.cpu-only: Host-side test without device execution. It runs with every build and is never counted as translated GPU execution.
categories.windows-specific: Direct3D 12, DXGI, DXC/DXIL or COM interop test. It is retained in the original Windows baseline and not executed on translated targets.

deviceRowPolicy: Translated targets expose one device. The test adapter maps both upstream Device values to it, so every upstream row executes once per target profile and reports the actual device and whether it is hardware or software. The original baseline executes WARP rows; Discrete rows need a hardware adapter and may be inconclusive on hosted runners.

fp64.description: Double-precision shader arithmetic. Metal Shading Language has no double type; OpenGL 4.0 core and later provide it (verified at runtime, never assumed).

rw-texture-rgb32.description: Typed read-write textures with three 32-bit channels. DXGI R32G32B32 formats have no typed UAV support, Metal has no three-channel 32-bit pixel formats, and OpenGL image load/store has no three-channel formats. Every other ComputeSharp read-write texture element type is required on every profile.

ComputeSharp.Tests.DeviceLost.DeviceDisp.reason: Disposes Direct3D 12 devices with and without live buffers, textures and shaders and checks the ID3D12Device COM reference count after each step.

ComputeSharp.Tests.DeviceLost.DeviceLost.reason: Removes the device through ID3D12Device5::RemoveDevice and checks that the DeviceLost event is raised once and that buffer and texture allocations and capability queries on the removed device throw InvalidOperationException.

ComputeSharp.Tests.DeviceLost.GetDefault.reason: Checks that GraphicsDevice.GetDefault caches the Direct3D 12 device, survives device removal and returns a new device on the same adapter LUID after disposal.

history.change: Initial freeze of the DeviceLost inventory, retained on the original Windows WARP baseline only.
